extracted.intended_audience: owners/operators of affected electric generating units (EGUs), designated representatives, plant environmental/compliance staff, and permitting/reporting personnel
extracted.subtask_description: Procedures and requirements for monitoring, calculating, reporting, and recordkeeping to demonstrate compliance with EPA CO2 emissions standards for affected EGUs (output- or heat-input-based), including instrumentation, calculations, reporting timing, and retention. Covers CEMS, alternative methods for liquid/gaseous fuels, apportionment, and compliance-demonstration procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modified steam generating unit emission limit
rubrics_metrics.description: For modified steam generating units, you must not discharge from the affected EGU any gases that contain CO2 in excess of 230 lb CO2/MMBtu.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring plan preparation and submission
rubrics_metrics.description: For affected sources (except certain combustion turbines), you must prepare a monitoring plan to quantify the hourly CO2 mass emission rate (tons/h) in accordance with the applicable provisions in 40 CFR 75.53(g) and (h). The electronic portion must be submitted using the ECMPS Client Tool and must be in place prior to reporting emissions data and/or monitoring system certification test results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitoring plan must be updated as necessary. Monitoring plan submittals must be made by the Designated Representative (DR), the Alternate DR, or a delegated agent of the DR (see §60.5555a(d) and (e)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Hourly CO2 mass emissions determination (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: You must determine the hourly CO2 mass emissions in kg from your affected EGU(s) according to paragraphs (b)(1) through (5) of this section, or, if applicable, as provided in paragraph (c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use either continuous monitoring (CEMS/flow) methods in (b) or alternative heat-input/fuel-based methods in (c) as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: CEMS requirement for coal-fired EGUs
rubrics_metrics.description: For an affected EGU that combusts coal you must install, certify, operate, maintain, and calibrate a CO2 continuous emission monitoring system (CEMS) to directly measure and record hourly average CO2 concentrations and a flow monitoring system to measure hourly average stack gas flow rates, according to 40 CFR 75.10(a)(3)(i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As an alternative to direct CO2 concentration measurement (if EGU does not use carbon separation), you may use data from a certified O2 monitor to calculate CO2 concentration in accordance with 40 CFR 75.10(a)(3)(iii).

rubrics_metrics.name: CEMS moisture monitoring when measuring dry-basis CO2
rubrics_metrics.description: If you measure CO2 concentration on a dry basis, you must also install, certify, operate, maintain, and calibrate a continuous moisture monitoring system, according to 40 CFR 75.11(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternatively, you may use an appropriate fuel-specific default moisture value from 40 CFR 75.11(b) or submit a petition to the Administrator under 40 CFR 75.66 for a site-specific default moisture value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification and QA for continuous monitoring systems
rubrics_metrics.description: For each continuous monitoring system used to determine CO2 mass emissions, you must meet the applicable certification and quality assurance procedures in 40 CFR 75.20 and appendices A and B to 40 CFR part 75.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of unadjusted exhaust gas volumetric flow rates
rubrics_metrics.description: You must use only unadjusted exhaust gas volumetric flow rates to determine the hourly CO2 mass emissions rate; you must not apply the bias adjustment factors described in Section 7.6.5 of appendix A to 40 CFR part 75 to the exhaust gas flow rate data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference method and flow RATA setup/calibration
rubrics_metrics.description: You must select an appropriate reference method to set up (characterize) the flow monitor and to perform the on-going RATAs in accordance with 40 CFR part 75. If you use a Type-S pitot tube or assembly for flow RATAs, you must calibrate it and you may not use the 0.84 default Type-S pitot tube coefficient specified in Method 2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hourly CO2 mass emissions calculation steps (CEMS/flow)
rubrics_metrics.description: Calculate the hourly CO2 mass emissions (kg) only for 'valid operating hours' by: (i) beginning with the hourly CO2 mass emission rate (tons/h) from Equation F-11 in appendix F to 40 CFR part 75 (wet basis) or section 4.2 of appendix F (dry basis); (ii) multiply hourly tons/h by EGU operating time in hours to get tons CO2; (iii) multiply by 907.2 to convert tons to kg and round to the nearest kg.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hourly CO2 tons/h values and EGU (or stack) operating times used to calculate CO2 mass emissions are required to be recorded under 40 CFR 75.57(e) and must be reported electronically under 40 CFR 75.64(a)(6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative method for liquid/gaseous fuel EGUs (heat-input approach)
rubrics_metrics.description: If your affected EGU exclusively combusts liquid fuel and/or gaseous fuel, you may determine hourly CO2 mass emissions by implementing procedures in appendix D to 40 CFR part 75 to determine hourly heat input rates (MMBtu/h) and then use Equation G-4 in appendix G to calculate hourly CO2 mass emission rate (tons/h).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may determine site-specific carbon-based F-factors (Fc) using Equation F-7b in appendix F and use these instead of default Fc values. For each valid operating hour multiply tons/h by operating time and convert to kg, rounding to the nearest two significant figures. Record/report per 40 CFR 75.57(e) and 75.64(a)(6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-uniform fuel combustion turbine alternative methods
rubrics_metrics.description: If you operate a combustion turbine firing non-uniform fuels, you may determine CO2 emissions during the compliance period using either: (i) the procedure under §60.107a(d) (units firing fuel gas) and convert heat input to CO2 using Equation G-4; or (ii) the Tier 3 methodology under 40 CFR 98.33(a)(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Determine emissions-basis (output vs heat-input)
rubrics_metrics.description: You must determine the basis of the emissions standard that applies (output-based or heat-input-based) and follow the respective measurement and calculation procedures in paragraph (d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choice affects whether you must meter electrical output (output-based) or calculate heat input per fuel (heat-input-based), and influences apportionment and compliance calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Watt meters and metering for output-based standards
rubrics_metrics.description: If subject to an output-based standard, you must install, calibrate, maintain, and operate a sufficient number of watt meters to continuously measure and record hourly gross or net electric output using 0.2 class electricity metering instrumentation and calibration procedures as specified under ANSI No. C12.20-2010.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For CHP EGUs you must also meter total useful thermal output continuously. For process steam applications, install meters to continuously determine and record hourly steam flow rate, temperature, and pressure. Your plan must ensure installation and hourly recording of each component of the determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heat-input basis monitoring for non-uniform heating-value fuels
rubrics_metrics.description: If subject to a heat-input standard and using non-uniform heating value fuels, you must determine total heat input for each fuel during the compliance period using one of: (i) Appendix D to 40 CFR part 75; (ii) procedures under §60.107a(d); or (iii) convert CO2 emissions to heat input using appropriate emission factor in table C-1 of 40 CFR part 98 or a site-specific Fc per EPA Method 19 and Equation G-4.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apportionment for EGUs serving a common electric generator
rubrics_metrics.description: If two or more affected EGUs serve a common electric generator, apportion the combined hourly gross or net energy output to individual EGUs according to the fraction of the total steam load and/or direct mechanical energy contributed by each EGU; alternatively, if EGUs are identical, apportion by fraction of total heat input.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may elect alternate methods if demonstrated satisfactory to the Administrator; Administrator may approve alternate methods that ensure accurate estimation of emissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring when EGUs share a common exhaust stack
rubrics_metrics.description: If two or more affected EGUs implementing continuous monitoring share a common stack you must monitor hourly CO2 mass emissions either: (1) at the common stack in lieu of monitoring each EGU separately if the EGUs are subject to the same emissions standard in table 1 (hourly gross/net energy output must be the sum of individual loads and operating time expressed as 'stack operating hours'); or (2) monitor each EGU separately prior to mixing or apportion CO2 based on load contribution and F-factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If compliance is attained at the common stack, each affected EGU sharing the stack is in compliance. Administrator may approve alternate apportionment methods upon satisfactory demonstration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring for multiple stacks or ducts
rubrics_metrics.description: If exhaust gases are emitted through multiple stacks (or routed to a common stack through multiple ducts and you elect to monitor in the ducts), you must monitor hourly CO2 mass emissions and 'stack operating time' at each stack or duct separately and determine compliance by summing measured emissions and dividing by total gross/net energy output for the affected EGU.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use only valid operating hours in compliance periods
rubrics_metrics.description: Each compliance period shall include only 'valid operating hours', i.e., operating hours for which: (i) 'valid data' are obtained for all parameters used to determine hourly CO2 mass emissions (and heat input if applicable); and (ii) the corresponding hourly gross or net energy output value is also valid data (hours with no useful output: zero is valid).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclude hours where substitute data provisions of part 75 are applied, exceedance of full-scale CEMS range occurs for any relevant parameters, or total gross/net energy output or heat input is unavailable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum percentage of valid operating hours
rubrics_metrics.description: For each compliance period, at least 95 percent of the operating hours in the compliance period must be valid operating hours.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total CO2 mass emissions calculation for compliance period
rubrics_metrics.description: Calculate total CO2 mass emissions by summing the valid hourly CO2 mass emissions values from §60.5535a for all valid operating hours in the compliance period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of hourly gross/net energy output (Pgross/net)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each valid operating hour used in emissions summation, you must determine Pgross/net (hourly gross or net energy output in MWh) according to specified equation components (Pe_ST, Pe_CT, Pe_IE, Pe_FW, Pe_A, Pt_PS, Pt_HR, Pt_IE) and apply the Transmission and Distribution Factor (TDF).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Convert each hourly gross/net energy output reported under part 75 to MWh by multiplying by EGU/stack operating time. For CHP and other applicable units, calculate Pt_PS per paragraph (a)(5)(ii) using measured thermal flow (Qm), enthalpy (H), and conversion factor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculate Pt_PS (useful steam thermal output) for CHP
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicable (e.g., CHP), calculate the useful thermal steam output (Pt_PS) for each hour using: Qm (measured useful thermal output flow in kg (lb)) × H (enthalpy at measured temp/pressure relative to SATP or condensate energy) then convert using CF = 3.6 × 10^9 J/MWh or 3.413 × 10^6 Btu/MWh.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basis calculation for actual annual emission rate
rubrics_metrics.description: Sources complying with output-based standards must calculate the denominator by summing hourly gross/net energy outputs for all valid operating hours in the compliance period. Sources complying with heat-input-based standards must calculate the total heat input for each fuel fired during the compliance period including all valid operating hours and consistent with fuel-specific procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compute CO2 mass emissions rate and rounding rules
rubrics_metrics.description: If output-based, divide total CO2 mass emissions by total gross/net energy output (kg/MWh) and round: two significant figures if <1,000; three significant figures if >1,000. If heat-input-based, divide total CO2 mass emissions by total heat input (kg/GJ or lb/MMBtu) and round to two significant figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: System emergency exclusion and emergency standards
rubrics_metrics.description: You may exclude CO2 mass emissions and output for hours during which the EGU operated during a system emergency (as defined in §60.5580a) if you provide the information listed in §60.5560a(i). While operating during a system emergency, compliance determination depends on subcategory: (i) intermediate or base load subcategory use low load combustion turbine standard; (ii) affected modified steam generating units' CO2 emission standard while operating during a system emergency is 230 lb CO2/MMBtu.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Records required to demonstrate system emergency are specified in §60.5560a(i).

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance criterion (must not exceed standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each 12-operating-month compliance period, the CO2 mass emissions rate determined per the procedures must be less than or equal to the applicable CO2 emissions standard in table 1 to this subpart or the emissions standard calculated per §60.5525a(a)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance date extension for certain new/reconstructed turbines
rubrics_metrics.description: New or reconstructed stationary combustion turbines in the base load subcategory installing add-on controls that cannot comply with Phase 2 CO2 standard by Jan 1, 2032 due to circumstances beyond control may request a compliance date extension of up to one year beyond Jan 1, 2032, and only once. The request must contain a demonstration of necessity with specific information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstration must identify units, describe controls, document progress (contracts, permits), identify circumstances beyond control with evidence (vendor/engineering info, permit delays, CO2 pipeline delays), propose a compliance date no later than one year after applicable date. Submit no later than 6 months prior to applicable effective date; notify Administrator at submission time. Administrator approves/disapproves based on written determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notifications to submit
rubrics_metrics.description: You must prepare and submit the notifications specified in §§60.7(a)(1) and (3) and 60.19, as applicable to your affected EGU(s) (see table 3 to this subpart), and the notifications specified in 40 CFR 75.61, as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quarterly electronic reporting timing and frequency
rubrics_metrics.description: For affected EGUs required to conduct compliance determinations on a 12-operating-month rolling average basis, submit electronic quarterly reports after accumulating the first 12 operating months: submit the report for the calendar quarter that includes the twelfth operating month no later than 30 days after quarter end; thereafter submit a report each calendar quarter no later than 30 days after quarter end.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit reports using the ECMPS Client Tool.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quarterly report content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Each quarterly report must include, as applicable: (i) each rolling average CO2 mass emissions rate for which the last operating month falls within the quarter (calculated per §60.5540a) and the first/twelfth operating months' dates; (ii) identification of operating months in the calendar quarter where the EGU violated the applicable CO2 standard; (iii) statement if no violations; (iv) percentage of valid operating hours in each 12-operating-month compliance period; (v) CO2 emissions standard with which EGU must comply; (vi) indication whether hourly gross/net energy output values used are based solely on gross electrical load.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the final quarterly report of each calendar year include gross/net energy output sold to an electric grid over the four quarters and the potential electric output of the EGU.

rubrics_metrics.name: ECMPS submission requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: You must submit all electronic reports required under this section using the Emissions Collection and Monitoring Plan System (ECMPS) Client Tool provided by the Clean Air Markets Division.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting for Acid Rain Program participants and timing for new units
rubrics_metrics.description: Affected EGUs subject to the Acid Rain Program must meet applicable reporting under subpart G of part 75. Newly-constructed affected EGUs subject to Acid Rain must begin submitting quarterly electronic emissions reports beginning with data recorded on and after the earlier of: (A) date of provisional certification per 40 CFR 75.20(a)(3); or (B) 180 days after date EGU commences commercial operation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For newly-constructed affected EGUs not subject to Acid Rain, begin submitting quarterly reports beginning with data recorded on and after the date reporting is required to begin under 40 CFR 75.64(a) if that date occurs on or after May 23, 2023. For reconstructed/modified units, reporting begins when unit becomes affected, provided ECMPS Client Tool can receive/process net energy output; otherwise report on gross basis until Client Tool can receive net output.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim reporting when monitoring uncertified
rubrics_metrics.description: If any required monitoring system has not been provisionally certified by the date reporting must begin, the maximum (or in some cases, minimum) potential value for the measured parameter shall be reported until certification testing is successfully completed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operating hours using maximum potential values are not 'valid operating hours' and shall not be used in compliance determinations under §60.5540.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who must submit reports (DR/ADR/authorized persons)
rubrics_metrics.description: For EGUs subject to the Acid Rain Program, reports shall be submitted by the Designated Representative (DR) under 40 CFR 72.20, the Alternate DR under 40 CFR 72.22, or a person authorized by the DR/ADR under 40 CFR 72.26. For EGUs not subject to Acid Rain, the owner/operator shall appoint a DR and optionally an ADR to submit reports; DR/ADR must register with CAMD Business System and may delegate authority to others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting and handling when CO2 is captured
rubrics_metrics.description: If your affected EGU captures CO2 to meet the emission standard, you must report in accordance with 40 CFR part 98, subpart PP, and either: (1) report under subpart RR or VV if injection occurs on-site; (2) transfer captured CO2 to a facility that reports under subpart RR or VV if injection off-site; or (3) transfer to a facility that has received an innovative technology waiver from EPA pursuant to paragraph (g).

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of transfer-to-reporting-facility requirement for captured CO2
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person may request the Administrator to waive the requirement that captured CO2 be transferred to a facility reporting under part 98 subpart RR or VV. To receive a waiver, applicant must demonstrate technology will store captured CO2 as effectively as geologic sequestration and will not cause unreasonable risk to public health/welfare/safety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrator considers operating history, effect on other pollutant emissions, permanence of CO2 storage, may test system or require tests, may grant conditional approval with monitoring/reporting conditions, may withdraw approval on evidence of releases. Administrator will provide public notice of applications and proposed actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: General recordkeeping requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: You must maintain records of the information used to demonstrate compliance with this subpart as specified in §60.7(b) and (f).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping for EGUs subject to part 75 subpart F
rubrics_metrics.description: Affected EGUs subject to the Acid Rain Program must follow applicable recordkeeping requirements and maintain records under subpart F of part 75. Affected EGUs not in the Acid Rain Program must also follow subpart F recordkeeping to the extent those records provide applicable data for compliance demonstrations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regardless, at minimum, maintain the specific records listed in paragraph (b)(2) (monitoring plan records, operating parameter records, records for flow/moisture/CO2 concentration, oil/gas flow meters, QA records for CEMS and fuel flow meters, DAHS verification).

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific records to retain (minimum list)
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain, as applicable: monitoring plan records under 40 CFR 75.53(g) and (h); operating parameter records under 40 CFR 75.57(b)(1)-(4); stack gas volumetric flow rate records under 40 CFR 75.57(c)(2); moisture monitoring records under 40 CFR 75.57(c)(3); CO2 concentration or O2-derived CO2 records under 40 CFR 75.57(e)(1) (except e(1)(x)); oil and gas flow meter records per 75.58(c); QA records per 40 CFR 75.59(a) for CEMS and fuel flow meters; DAHS verification under 40 CFR 75.59(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Records of emissions calculations and outputs
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep records of calculations performed to determine hourly and total CO2 mass emissions (tons) for each operating month and each compliance period (including each 12-operating-month compliance period). Keep records of data and calculations used to determine gross or net energy output for each operating month, percentage of valid CO2 mass emission rates in each compliance period, compliance assessment calculations for applicable CO2 standards, and any site-specific carbon-based F-factors used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Records to determine subcategory and system emergency demonstration
rubrics_metrics.description: For stationary combustion turbines, keep records of electric sales to determine applicable subcategory. To demonstrate operation during a system emergency keep: (1) documentation that the system emergency was in effect from issuing entity and duration; (2) documentation that the emergency included the affected source/region; (3) documentation that facility was instructed to increase output beyond planned schedule or remain in operation outside scheduled dispatch from Reliability Coordinator, Balancing Authority, or ISO/RTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record form and retention period
rubrics_metrics.description: Records must be in a form suitable and readily available for expeditious review and each record must be maintained for 5 years after the date of conclusion of each compliance period.
